title: Home Mortgage Loans: Borrower Requests to Cancel Private Mortgage Insurance
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Borrower Requests to Cancel Private Mortgage Insurance

A borrower whose loan under Home Mortgage Loans carries private mortgage insurance (PMI) can ask for that insurance to be cancelled before it would end by itself. This page states what the request must satisfy and how each measure is taken.

## The requirements

A borrower-requested cancellation of PMI requires every one of the following:

- **Written request.** The borrower asks for cancellation in writing.
- **Loan-to-value.** The loan's current loan-to-value is at or below the program's request threshold.
- **Loan current.** The loan is current at the time of the request.
- **No 30-day lateness in the shorter look-back.** During the months of the program's 30-day look-back, counting back from the request, no payment was 30 or more days late.
- **No 60-day lateness in the longer look-back.** During the months of the program's 60-day look-back, counting back from the request, no payment was 60 or more days late.

## How the measures are taken

- **Current loan-to-value** is the unpaid principal divided by the original property value, expressed as a percentage to two decimal places. The denominator is always the value recorded at origination. A fresh appraisal, whatever it shows, is never substituted.
- **Payment lateness** is judged from the loan's late charge and payment history: for each month of the look-back, the greatest number of days past due that the loan reached in that month is taken.
- **Source of the facts.** Principal, original value and days past due are read from the bank's loan records.

## Truth table

| LTV at or below request threshold | Current now | Any 30-day lateness in shorter look-back | Any 60-day lateness in longer look-back | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | no | no | every requirement of this policy is met |
| no | any | any | any | not available: value test fails |
| yes | no | any | any | not available: loan not current |
| yes | yes | yes | any | not available: 30-day history test fails |
| yes | yes | any | yes | not available: 60-day history test fails |

## Worked measures (hypothetical loan)

- An imagined loan has unpaid principal of $318400.00 against an original property value of $400000.00. Dividing gives 79.60 percent. The borrower mentions a recent appraisal of $450000.00; that appraisal plays no part, and 79.60 percent is the figure compared with the request threshold.
- In the same imagined loan, one payment reached 45 days past due at a point inside the longer look-back but outside the shorter one. It is not a 60-day lateness, and it falls outside the window used for 30-day lateness, so neither history test is broken by it.

The balances, values and history above are invented for illustration.
